summary.text: CA9 is the candidate with the strongest and most robust convergent evidence. It leads the overall convergence ranking (score 4.5197) and is the only gene in the robust overall top ten. It is up in tumour at RNA (log2FC 6.312) and protein (log2FC 2.269), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 9.712), survives extrapolation to a pure tumour (RNA log2FC at purity 1 of 7.787), and single-cell data place 0.976 of its tissue transcripts in RCC cells. Girentuximab reached PHASE_3. Because DepMap shows no dependency (mean effect 0.051), its value is as a surface antigen for antibody, imaging or radioligand approaches and as a diagnostic biomarker, not as an essential pathway gene.

A second tier of surface or metabolic targets is consistently up in tumour, protein-confirmed, replicated in TCGA-KIRC and purity-robust: CD70, SCARB1, NNMT, ENPP3, SLC16A3 (MCT4) and HK2. CD70 and ENPP3 already have antibody or ADC programmes; NNMT has selective tool inhibitors in the literature and adverse prognosis in TCGA; SCARB1 tops the target profile but has no literature in the corpus and a mixed tumour, myeloid and endothelial single-cell profile. None of these candidates shows a selective DepMap dependency, so the target calls rest on tumour-restricted expression and tractability rather than essentiality.

The biomarker profile is led by genes lost with proximal-tubule identity: PSAT1, PCK1, ALDH6A1 and SLC6A19 (together with ALDOB and SLC22A8 in the overall ranking). They are down in tumour at RNA and protein, replicate in TCGA-KIRC and carry significant TCGA survival associations, which makes them diagnostic and prognostic candidates rather than therapeutic targets.

The clinically validated ccRCC axes appear as context rather than as data-led discoveries: VHL and PBRM1 are the dominant somatic drivers, EPAS1 (belzutifan, approved) is a selective but partial DepMap dependency, KDR is an endothelial angiogenesis target and MTOR is common-essential. Discovery candidates (COL23A1, RAB42 in tumour; OLFML2A in stroma; GAL3ST4 and LILRB4 in the immune track) are data-ranked hypotheses without dependency evidence.

omics.text: In CPTAC tumour-vs-normal data CA9 is the clearest up-regulated candidate: RNA log2FC 6.312 (padj 1.72e-49) and protein log2FC 2.269 (padj 9.9e-43).

Other tumour-up genes with protein confirmation are CD70 (RNA log2FC 4.464, protein 2.421), NNMT (RNA 4.67, protein 2.709), SCARB1 (RNA 2.974, protein 1.837), ENPP3 (RNA 3.895, protein 1.544), SLC16A3 (RNA 3.435, protein 2.279) and HK2 (RNA 3.351, protein 2.106). SLC16A3 also has a positive copy-number-to-RNA cis effect (rho 0.258).
On the loss side, ALDH6A1 is down at RNA (log2FC -3.399) and protein (log2FC -1.925), with CNV loss frequency 0.355 and a positive cis effect (rho 0.525), consistent with a 3p-linked dosage effect.
VHL loses a copy in 0.791 of tumours and is mutated in 247 of 511 patients (frequency 0.483), explaining the HIF-driven programme behind CA9 and NNMT.

literature.text: Literature support is concentrated on CA9 and CD70, the only candidates with translational imaging or antibody evidence in the corpus: CA9-targeted PET is described as proof-of-concept warranting prospective validation, and CD70 is reported as overexpressed in RCC with minimal normal-tissue expression and targeted by 68Ga-labelled single-domain antibodies. NNMT is described as a prognostic biomarker and potential target, with selective tool inhibitors from a medicinal-chemistry paper.

Most biomarker literature (ALDOB, SLC22A8, ENO2, FCER1G, PLIN2) rests on single recent bioinformatic or IHC studies without prospective validation. COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) has the densest mechanistic literature (HIF induction, glycolysis, ferroptosis) but is preclinical. The corpus also contains contradictions: MT1G is low in tumour yet linked to poor prognosis, and PFKP is up in tumour while low expression is linked to poor survival. SCARB1, PIGR, ENPP3 and EPAS1 have little or no extracted literature despite strong data or clinical support.

external.text: Open Targets drug records separate candidates with clinical programmes from untested ones. CA9 (girentuximab, PHASE_3), CD70 (cusatuzumab, PHASE_2) and ENPP3 (AGS-16C3F, PHASE_2) are antibody-accessible membrane proteins; NNMT and SCARB1 have predicted tractability only and no drugs listed.

EPAS1 (HIF-2alpha) is the established ccRCC target with belzutifan approved; DepMap shows a selective but partial dependency (ccRCC mean effect -0.143, selectivity 0.3, fraction of ccRCC lines dependent 0.208), consistent with heterogeneity of VHL loss.

MTOR is a dependency in every ccRCC line (mean effect -1.52, fraction 1.0) but is common-essential, so it offers no tumour selectivity and carries a toxicity risk. KDR is an approved angiogenesis target whose relevant cell is the endothelium, so tumour-cell DepMap data do not apply to it.

cells.text: CA9 is tumour-cell intrinsic: RCC cells hold 0.976 of its tissue transcripts (54.7% of RCC cells express it), and tumour cells versus proximal tubule give log2FC 7.739 (padj 0.0189).

SCARB1 is not purely tumour-intrinsic despite its bulk signal: macrophages hold 0.384 of its transcripts, RCC cells 0.336 and endothelium 0.116, with endothelium the highest per cell (cpm_share 0.406). It should be treated as a shared tumour, myeloid and endothelial signal.

Several bulk or clinical candidates are microenvironmental rather than tumour-intrinsic: KDR is endothelial (0.951 of transcripts), CD74 and CXCR4 are immune-borne, and EPAS1 transcripts in this scRNA-seq are mostly endothelial and fibroblast (RCC cells show 0.051 transcript share). By contrast MET (0.935) and EGFR (0.948) are mainly in tumour cells. CD70 single-cell records carried no evidence ids, so its cell-level split is not quoted.

spatial.text: In Visium sections, high-CA9 spots are enriched for RCC neighbours (log2 enrichment 0.381, padj 0.0017; observed 0.4757 vs expected 0.3654) and only weakly for macrophages (log2 0.099). The composition-corrected in situ share of CA9 transcripts is 0.999 RCC, confirming the single-cell assignment.

structure.text: Molecular-glue-degrader scores rank candidate sites; they are not evidence that a degrader exists. CA9's best site scores only 0.546 (cavity volume 126.8 A3, pocket pLDDT 90.3, 1 accessible lysine), with ligand-site recall 0.5, a modest site for a protein already addressed by antibodies.

KDR has a higher site score (0.841; pocket volume 361.1 A3, 7 accessible lysines), but ligand-site recall is 0.4 and mean model pLDDT 71.12, and the relevant cell would be the endothelium rather than the tumour.

discovery.text: In the tumour track, COL23A1 is the leading first-in-class candidate (novelty 0.767): RCC cells hold 0.881 of tumour transcripts, it has no clinical drug, is surface or secreted and antibody/PROTAC-tractable, and has low vital-organ expression (max nTPM 3). It replicates in TCGA (log2FC 5.829) and survives purity extrapolation (rna_lfc_at_purity1 4.88). Its AlphaFold model is low confidence (mean pLDDT 58.91) and there is no dependency evidence (DepMap mean effect 0.167).

RAB42 is the second tumour-track candidate (novelty 0.705; RCC holds 0.627 of tumour transcripts; only 2 ccRCC papers). TCGA log2FC 4.371 and rna_lfc_at_purity1 3.189 support tumour-intrinsic expression, but there is no selective dependency (DepMap mean effect -0.075) and its best glue site is small.

The stromal and immune tracks are weaker. OLFML2A is fibroblast-held (0.647 of tumour transcripts) with notable colon expression. In the immune pool, GAL3ST4 is macrophage-held (0.972) and its TCGA log2FC 2.993 shrinks to 0.401 at purity 1, and LILRB4 (TCGA log2FC 3.7, 0.508 at purity 1) is flagged infiltration-driven: both bulk signals mostly vanish in a pure tumour. All discovery candidates remain data-ranked hypotheses; none is a selective dependency.

validation.text: External replication in TCGA-KIRC strengthens all leading tumour-up candidates: CA9 (log2FC 9.712), CD70 (7.09), ENPP3 (5.557), NNMT (4.685), SCARB1 (3.989), HK2 (3.974) and SLC16A3 (3.291). The purity check confirms they are tumour-intrinsic, with RNA log2FC at purity 1 of 7.787 (CA9), 4.278 (CD70), 5.278 (ENPP3), 5.256 (NNMT), 3.762 (SCARB1), 3.989 (HK2) and 3.821 (SLC16A3). In contrast, immune-held genes such as LILRB4 lose most of their bulk change at purity 1.

Prognosis separates candidates. NNMT associates with worse survival (Cox log HR 0.301, padj 0.00479), and the tubule-identity genes carry strong survival signals (PCK1 Cox log HR -0.415, padj 1.91e-7; SLC6A19 -0.456, padj 1.07e-7; ALDH6A1 -0.554, padj 9.45e-12; ALDOB -0.358). CA9 and SCARB1 have no prognostic signal, which weakens them as prognostic markers but not as diagnostic or targeting candidates.

Somatic driver status and dependency weaken the case for most data-led targets as essential genes: only VHL (frequency 0.483) and PBRM1 (frequency 0.362) are recurrent drivers, and the only selective DepMap dependency among discussed genes is EPAS1, which is partial; MTOR is common-essential. Kinase activity analyses were not run for these candidates.

robustness.text: Under random re-weighting of the target profile, SCARB1 (p_top10 0.968, 90% rank interval 1 to 8), CA9 (p_top10 0.941), SLC16A3 (0.881), CD70 (0.88), NNMT (0.88) and ENPP3 (0.823) stay in the top ten in most draws and form the robust target core; HK2 (0.697) is less stable. In the overall convergence ranking only CA9 is robust (p_top10 0.894, p_top25 0.983), while SCARB1 drops further (rank_p95 31) because its literature support is thin.

In the biomarker profile PSAT1 is the most stable call (p_top10 0.986, rank_p95 4), followed by PCK1 (0.889) and SLC6A19 (0.881). ALDH6A1 (p_top10 0.773) has a wide interval (rank_p05 1 to rank_p95 33) and NNMT's biomarker rank depends more on the chosen weights (p_top10 0.619) than its target rank does.

integration.text: Omics, literature and external knowledge converge most clearly on CA9 and CD70: both are tumour-up, replicated, purity-robust membrane antigens with clinical antibody programmes and translational literature. NNMT is the best-supported candidate without a clinical drug, combining omics, adverse prognosis and published tool inhibitors.

The layers disagree on SCARB1 and the HIF axis. SCARB1 tops the data-driven target profile yet has no extracted literature and a mixed single-cell origin; EPAS1 is clinically validated but ranks low in the data, has no extracted literature in the corpus and is mostly stromal in scRNA-seq. These disagreements show that convergence scoring favours tumour-restricted expression and should be read alongside established biology rather than replacing it.

targets.rationale: Top of the overall ranking and robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.941). Tumour-cell intrinsic (0.976 of transcripts in RCC cells), replicated in TCGA (log2FC 9.712), purity-robust, membrane-accessible, girentuximab PHASE_3. No DepMap dependency, so its value is as an antibody/radioligand antigen and diagnostic marker.

Robust target-profile member (p_top10 0.88): up at RNA (log2FC 4.464) and protein (2.421), TCGA log2FC 7.09, purity-robust, with antibody/ADC programmes and translational literature. Ranked above SCARB1 by judgment because its clinical and literature support is far stronger; part of its signal may be lymphocyte-derived.

Up at RNA (log2FC 4.67) and protein (2.709), replicated (TCGA log2FC 4.685), purity-robust and associated with worse survival (Cox log HR 0.301). Selective tool inhibitors exist in the literature but no clinical drug.
Up at RNA (log2FC 3.895) and protein (1.544), TCGA log2FC 5.557, purity-robust (5.278), robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.823), with the ADC AGS-16C3F at PHASE_2.

MCT4: up at RNA (log2FC 3.435) and protein (2.279), replicated (TCGA log2FC 3.291), purity-robust (3.821), positive cis dosage effect, robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.881); no drugs yet.

Glycolytic enzyme up at RNA (log2FC 3.351) and protein (2.106), replicated (TCGA log2FC 3.974) and purity-robust (3.989); no selective dependency and a less stable target-profile position (p_top10 0.697).

Included despite a low data rank because it is the clinically validated ccRCC target (belzutifan approved) and the only selective, if partial, DepMap dependency here (fraction of ccRCC lines dependent 0.208). Its scRNA-seq transcripts are mostly stromal.
Most robust biomarker (score 5.3696, p_top10 0.986): down at RNA (log2FC -3.867) and protein (-1.963), replicated in TCGA (log2FC -2.974), with a significant survival association (padj 5.66e-7).
Down at RNA (log2FC -4.424) and protein (-1.859), replicated (TCGA log2FC -3.079), higher expression protective (Cox log HR -0.415, padj 1.91e-7); robust in the biomarker profile (p_top10 0.889).
Proximal-tubule transporter down at RNA (log2FC -4.574) and protein (-1.48), replicated (TCGA log2FC -3.221), protective (Cox log HR -0.456); robust in the biomarker profile (p_top10 0.881).

limitations.text: No data-led target candidate shows a selective DepMap dependency in ccRCC lines; target calls rest on expression, tumour restriction and tractability rather than essentiality.
Literature relations are LLM-extracted from abstracts; most biomarker claims come from single bioinformatic or IHC studies, and several contain direction contradictions (MT1G, ABAT, PFKP).
Agents read only part of the convergence output because of size limits, and phosphosite and kinase-activity analyses were not run for the candidates.
Single-cell records for CD70 and NNMT carried no evidence ids, CD70 is not covered by the Visium sections, and proximal-tubule reference cells are few, limiting tumour-vs-tubule comparisons.
Molecular-glue-degrader scores rank structural sites only; ligand-site recall is modest where checkable and unavailable for discovery genes.
Discovery candidates are hypotheses ranked from data; literature novelty is counted by gene symbol and none has functional validation.
